method: Licences were verified by web search against project sources. Anything not verified is marked UNKNOWN rather than inferred. Maturity and production evidence are recorded only where a source stated them.

license_classes.B_REUSE_WITH_CONDITIONS: copyleft or content licence conditions apply
license_classes.C_STUDY_OR_ISOLATED_SERVICE: no code reuse; separate process only

candidates.architecture_risk: HIGH if adopted as store — would become a second source of truth for patient and clinical records, which GULA forbids
candidates.expected_value: HIGH as a reference for FHIR resource modelling and access policies
candidates.capability: FHIR R4 datastore, SMART on FHIR auth, access policies, subscriptions
candidates.gula_gap: GULA has a 6-file fhir package, no FHIR-native datastore
candidates.decision: STUDY — adopt its FHIR resource shapes and access-policy model; do not adopt its datastore

candidates.architecture_risk: LOW if used as a validation/translation sidecar behind an explicit boundary; Java runtime is an operational cost
candidates.expected_value: HIGH — conformance without writing a validator
candidates.gula_gap: No FHIR validation or $validate endpoint in GULA
candidates.decision: INTEGRATE as a stateless validation service; never as a datastore

candidates.architecture_risk: LOW — terminology is reference data, not a source of truth for patients
candidates.capability: SNOMED CT terminology server on Elasticsearch; Snowstorm Lite is a FHIR terminology server
candidates.gula_gap: GULA has NO terminology package at all — backend/app/terminology has 0 files
candidates.decision: INTEGRATE the code, but the SNOMED CT *content* licence is separate from Apache-2.0 and depends on Iraq's SNOMED International member status, which is UNKNOWN and needs legal confirmation before any use

candidates.production_evidence: National deployments across many ministries of health
candidates.architecture_risk: HIGH if adopted wholesale — DHIS2 is aggregate-first, GULA is transaction-first
candidates.expected_value: HIGH as a reference for indicator and dashboard modelling
candidates.capability: Aggregate health information system, national reporting, dashboards
candidates.gula_gap: GULA nhdw is 14/14 physical but has no aggregate reporting model
candidates.decision: STUDY its data-element/indicator model; do not run it as a parallel system

candidates.architecture_risk: LOW — a projection, explicitly not a source of truth
candidates.expected_value: HIGH for national analytics and research
candidates.capability: Observational research common data model and analytics tooling
candidates.gula_gap: GULA has no OMOP mapping; grep finds zero references
candidates.decision: ADAPT as a read-only projection from the warehouse; per-tool licences must be checked individually

candidates.architecture_risk: HIGH as a system; LOW as a model reference
candidates.expected_value: HIGH — its concept dictionary is a solved problem GULA has not solved
candidates.gula_gap: GULA EHR is 18 tables, none physical
candidates.decision: STUDY the concept dictionary and encounter model. MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft: any reused file stays MPL

candidates.architecture_risk: HIGH — would duplicate a domain GULA already owns
candidates.expected_value: MEDIUM — mainly its public-health lab reporting patterns
candidates.capability: Laboratory information system for clinical and public-health labs, FHIR R4 native
candidates.gula_gap: GULA lims is 35/35 physical and already reconciled
candidates.decision: STUDY only. GULA's LIMS is further along than adopting this would leave it

candidates.production_evidence: Reference technology for the OpenHIE architecture
candidates.expected_value: HIGH for the national exchange layer
candidates.capability: Health information exchange interoperability layer: routing, mediation, audit of cross-system transactions
candidates.gula_gap: GULA integration package (10 files) is bespoke
candidates.decision: STUDY the OpenHIE component pattern — it is the closest published architecture to what GULA's national layer needs

candidates.expected_value: HIGH for offline conflict resolution patterns
candidates.capability: Offline-first frontline health worker data collection and case management
candidates.gula_gap: GULA edge_agent and edge package exist (10 files) but offline sync is unproven at scale
candidates.decision: STUDY its offline sync and conflict model; GULA keeps its own edge agent

candidates.production_evidence: Widely used in hospitals and research
candidates.architecture_risk: MEDIUM. Running it as a separate process communicating over DICOM/REST is mere aggregation and does not impose GPL on GULA. Linking to it, or embedding an AGPL plugin, would. AGPL also reaches network use.
candidates.expected_value: HIGH — image storage is not worth building
candidates.gula_gap: GULA has radiology/pacs.py but no image store
candidates.decision: INTEGRATE as a separate service over DICOMweb only. Never link, never embed, never fork into the repository

candidates.architecture_risk: MEDIUM — the LGPL arm permits library use, the GPL arm does not
candidates.decision: Alternative to Orthanc if a full archive is needed; heavier
STUDY only. GPL makes code reuse incompatible with GULA's licensing posture; PHP stack is a poor fit

candidates.production_evidence: None found — the visible projects are coursework and demos
candidates.license: Mixed, mostly MIT on student projects
candidates.gula_gap: None. GULA blood bank has a real state machine, crossmatch verification and a two-person transfusion rule
candidates.decision: REJECT. GULA's blood bank is materially ahead of what is publicly available

candidates.maturity: UNKNOWN — SourceForge hosted, activity not verified
candidates.expected_value: MEDIUM — NEMSIS is the useful part, not the code
candidates.capability: NEMSIS-compliant EMS suite: dispatch, crew scheduling, field data collection
candidates.gula_gap: GULA ems is 12/12 physical with 26 operations
candidates.decision: STUDY the NEMSIS data model. Do not adopt code with an unverified licence

candidates.capability: UNVERIFIED — the site is blocked by this environment's egress proxy. Search results state only a mission to 'build tools that will improve access and quality of healthcare' and a care portal at care.gulahealth.com
candidates.decision: STUDY publicly observable product patterns only, once the site can actually be read. No relationship of any kind exists or is implied between Gula Health and the GULA Platform. Name similarity is coincidental. No code may be copied.
